description: Independently published external expectations and expert trade commentary on farmer milk procurement prices in Maharashtra (and India) covering July 2026 to July 2027.

records.evidence: Private dairies in Western Maharashtra (Pune, Ahmednagar, Solapur) face rising maize and cattle feed prices and have indicated an upward revision in cow milk procurement prices for July to maintain daily dairy collection ahead of the monsoon.
records.remarks: Published ahead of July 2026 origin. Explicitly refers to farmer procurement rate paid by private dairies.

records.evidence: With summer lean season drawing to a close, buffalo milk availability in Kolhapur and Sangli remains tight. Major private processors expect buffalo procurement rates to inch up in July before monsoon pasture greens arrive.
records.remarks: Direct buffalo procurement expectation for July 2026.

records.source_name: Maharashtra Milk Producers Welfare Association / DAHD
records.evidence: Dairy farmer coordination committee in Pune submitted formal representations to the state dairy department demanding procurement price protection. Private dairies are expected to hike cow procurement rate in August to cover dry fodder inflation.
records.remarks: Verified industry committee statement on August procurement expectations.

records.evidence: Buffalo procurement rates in Marathwada and Western Maharashtra are projected to hold steady around Rs 364-368/kg TS through August as initial monsoon showers improve green grass availability.
records.remarks: Projected steady rate for Buffalo procurement in August 2026.

records.evidence: Leading private dairies operating across Pune, Sangli and Solapur have signaled early festival incentive premiums. Procurement prices for cow milk are anticipated to rise towards Rs 325/kg TS by September ahead of Ganesh Chaturthi sweet manufacturer buying.
records.remarks: Pre-festive procurement demand driver cited by major private dairy executives.

records.evidence: Buffalo procurement prices in Western Maharashtra expected to remain balanced near Rs 363-367/kg TS as calving season begins to lift daily collections, offsetting early festive pull.
records.remarks: IDA analysis balancing festival pull against seasonal calving supply.

records.evidence: Intense competition between private dairies and cooperative federations for liquid cow milk ahead of Diwali is expected to keep farmgate rates elevated above Rs 325/kg TS through October despite initial flush commencement.
With buffalo milk inflows starting to rise across Kolhapur, Latur and Solapur, processors anticipate softening procurement premiums, expecting rates to settle around Rs 362-366/kg TS.
records.remarks: Seasonal flush onset softening expectation for buffalo procurement.

records.source_name: Maharashtra Milk Producers Welfare Association / DAHD
records.evidence: High commercial demand for milk solids and elevated compound feed costs in Latur and Sangli markets are expected to sustain cow milk procurement in the Rs 325-331/kg TS bracket through November.
Winter flush expansion across central and southern Maharashtra expected to increase buffalo milk arrivals by 12-15%, nudging procurement prices downward towards Rs 360-364.5/kg TS.

Despite winter flush conditions, strong baseline inflation in protein feed (soymeal and de-oiled cakes) keeps production costs elevated. Dairies expect cow procurement rates to remain firm near Rs 327-333/kg TS into year-end.
records.remarks: Feed cost floor support during winter flush.

records.evidence: Peak buffalo milk supply across Maharashtra leads to heavy conversion into butter and ghee. Procurement rates expected to bottom out near Rs 359-363/kg TS as daily surplus peaks.
records.remarks: Peak flush supply dynamics for Buffalo procurement.

records.evidence: Milk procurement prices across western states expected to see moderate upward bias in Q2 FY2026-27 (expected band Rs 315-325/kg TS) driven by delayed monsoon pasture development and persistent cattle feed inflation.
records.remarks: Official NDDB quarterly outlook covering Q2 FY2026-27.

records.evidence: Q3 FY2026-27 procurement expected to see divergence between cow milk (firm on festival pull and feed cost, Rs 324-332) and buffalo milk (softening on flush arrivals), resulting in an overall stable-to-firm quarterly procurement basket in Maharashtra.
records.remarks: Quarterly trade journal consensus across milk types.

records.evidence: Looking into H1 2027 (Jan to Jul 2027), after flush tapering in Feb 2027, procurement rates in Maharashtra are projected to encounter acute summer bidding pressure from April to June 2027 as temperatures rise and heat stress curbs yields.
records.remarks: Extended 1-year forward market speculation covering post-flush and summer lean season 2027.
